translationRepairs: Confucius and the Zhou sages left such matters unspoken, and truth and falsehood became impossible to sort out.
The Duke of Zhou and Confucius set these matters aside without discussing them, and truth and falsehood became impossible to sort out.
周、孔 is the Duke of Zhou and Confucius, not plural Zhou sages; 存而不論 means they preserved the matters without discussing them.
the martial power of Han had strong soldiers and horses and indulged its will in far-reaching designs.
Han Wudi had strong soldiers and horses and indulged his will in far-reaching designs.
漢武 parallels 秦皇 and names Emperor Wu of Han; the literal reading as abstract Han martial power breaks the parallel.
when tribute horses arrived at court, the common people were exhausted as well.
when dogs and horses had come in tribute, their people were exhausted as well.
犬馬 is dogs and horses, not horses alone, and 其民 refers to the people of the Xiongnu just named.

How much worse when rulers were no Qin or Han emperors yet aspired like Ying Zheng and the Liu emperors—defying Heaven's way for glory, draining the people for private ends: ruin would follow in no time at all.

How much worse when rulers were no Qin or Han emperors yet the ambition exceeded that of the Ying and the Liu—defying Heaven's way for glory, draining the people for private ends: ruin would follow in no time at all.
志甚嬴、劉 means the will went beyond the Ying and Liu houses; 甚 is exceeded, and 嬴 is the Ying house parallel to 劉, not the personal name Ying Zheng alone.
the royal domain from north to south barely acknowledged cave-dwellers and Jiaozhi.
the Royal Regulations, from north to south, barely named cave-dwellers and Jiaozhi.
王制 is the Royal Regulations, as the literal field has it, not the royal domain; 裁稱 means barely named.
The city measured six li east to west and stood on the Yalu River to the south.
The city measured six li east to west and faced the Pae River on the south.
浿水 is the Pae River, not the Yalu.
The city was six li from east to west and faced the Yalu River on the south.
The city was six li from east to west and faced the Pae River on the south.
浿水 is the Pae River, not the Yalu.
They revered Buddhism and especially favored extravagant cult sacrifices.
They revered Buddhism and especially favored unorthodox cult sacrifices.
淫祀 is the set term for illicit or unorthodox sacrifices, not extravagant ones.
隸焉 means the people were attached as subordinates; the literal transliterates the emended character 隸 as Li.
Si robes, with sleeves slightly large.
They were like robes, with slightly large sleeves.
似袍 means robe-like garments; the literal transliterates the emended character 似 as Si.
Fan proliferated, scattered between the Yangzi and Huai, in the commanderies of Ru and Yu.
They proliferated, scattered between the Yangzi and Huai, in the commanderies of Ru and Yu.
蕃衍 means they multiplied; Fan is the collation note's rejected character, not the verb.
From the time the southern dynasties held the lands east of the Yangzi and Later Wei held the Central Plains, both courts sent envoys declaring vassalage and both received titles and appointments.
From the time the southern dynasties held the lands east of the Yangzi and Later Wei held the Central Plains, Baekje sent envoys declaring itself a vassal and also received titles and appointments.
The subject of 遣使稱藩，兼受封拜 is Baekje, continued from this account, not the southern courts and Later Wei who are only the chronological setting.

From the time Jin, Song, Qi, and Liang held the lands east of the Yangzi and Later Wei occupied the Central Plains, both sides sent envoys declaring vassalage and both received enfeoffments and appointments.

From the time Jin, Song, Qi, and Liang held the lands east of the Yangzi and Later Wei occupied the Central Plains, they sent envoys declaring vassalage and also received enfeoffments and appointments.
竝遣使稱藩，兼受封拜 has Baekje as subject; Jin, Song, Qi, Liang, and Later Wei are the powers of that age, not the envoys' senders.
In the first year of  Lu Teng was ordered to command Wang Liang, Sima Yi, and others against them.
In the first year of Tianhe, Lu Teng was ordered to command Wang Liang, Sima Yi, and others against them.
The idiomatic drops 天和; the literal correctly has the first year of Tianhe.
Neighboring governor Pu Wei also rebelled.
The Governor of Lin Prefecture, Pu Wei, also rebelled.
鄰州刺史 is the governorship of Lin Prefecture, parallel to the other prefecture titles, not a nameless neighboring governor.
The neighboring prefecture governor Pu Wei also raised troops in defiance.
The Governor of Lin Prefecture, Pu Wei, also raised troops in defiance.
鄰州 is the prefecture name Linzhou; rendering 鄰 only as neighboring erases the office.
He won over Boli with gifts and sworn brotherhood.
He won over Boli with gifts and a sworn father-son bond.
結為父子 is a sworn father-and-son tie, not brotherhood.
Several live Liao chieftains came to Wenbiao and said, "We fear the government troops do not know the mountains and rivers—please serve as our guides."
Several live Liao chieftains came to Wenbiao and said, "We fear the government troops do not know the mountains and rivers—please let us serve as guides."
請為鄉導 is the Liao chiefs offering themselves as guides, not asking the army to guide them.
有梁 starts the personal name 梁勤; it is not a Liang clan.
Qin clan had long been chieftains, won the Qiang chiefs'loyalty, and called themselves kings.
Qin, whose line had long produced chieftains, won the Qiang nobles' hearts and styled himself king.
勤 is the given name Qin of one man, 梁勤, who styled himself king; it is not a Qin clan in the plural.
Qin clan that for generations were chieftains, winning the Qiang nobles'hearts, and styled themselves kings.
Qin, who for generations had been chieftain, winning the Qiang nobles' hearts, and styled himself king.
有梁勤者 is one man; 自稱王 is singular.
In Zhou they joined Yong, Shu, Wei, Lu, and six other states in overthrowing Shang.
In Zhou times, with Yong, Shu, Wei, Lu and the others, eight states in all, they followed King Wu to destroy Shang.
The idiomatic omits 武王; the Qiang forebears followed King Wu to destroy Shang, and 等八國 is eight states in all.
In Zhou times they with Yong, Shu, Wei, Lu and the other eight states followed King Wu to destroy Shang.
In Zhou times they with Yong, Shu, Wei, Lu and the others, eight states in all, followed King Wu to destroy Shang.
等八國 means eight states including those named, not eight states besides them.
In year 16 the Liao Gan seized his throne and Mideng fled to court.
In year 16 his clansman Liao Gan seized his position and Mideng fled to court.
The idiomatic drops 宗人, so Liao Gan is not identified as Mideng's clansman.
Earlier Qiang chiefs had seized Qulin Valley during Xianding's revolt with Zheng Wuchou stirring the Qiang.
Earlier the Qiang chieftain Bangqi Tieceng and others seized Qulin Valley during Xianding's revolt, and the Weizhou man Zheng Wuchou stirred the Qiang.
The idiomatic omits 傍乞鐵匆, who is named in the Chinese.
Yuwen Gui and others defeated the Liao Gan, executed the ringleaders, and restored Mideng.
An edict ordered Grand General Yuwen Gui, Dou Lu Ning, and Liang Prefecture Governor Shi Ning to attack the Liao Gan and the others; they captured and beheaded them, installed Mideng, and returned.
The idiomatic omits Dou Lu Ning and Shi Ning and the edict.
Later Qiang chiefs Dong Nianjie and Gong Lian rebelled; Dou Lu Ning and Wang Yong suppressed them.
Later Qiang chiefs Dong Nianjie, Gong Lian, and Juhe rebelled; Grand Generals Dou Lu Ning and Wang Yong suppressed them in turn.
The idiomatic omits 俱和 and flattens 前後, which means in turn.
In year 4 Mideng raided Min; Li Xian repulsed him.
In year 4 Mideng raided Tao Prefecture; Li Xian repulsed him.
洮州 is Tao Prefecture, not Min.
In the fourth year Mideng raided Min Prefecture and Commander Li Xian drove him off.
In the fourth year Mideng raided Tao Prefecture and Commander Li Xian drove him off.
洮州 is Tao Prefecture, not Min.
Xiang Shuzhi's line ruled Baishui and called themselves kings.
Xiang Shuzhi's line ruled Baishui and he styled himself king.
自稱 is singular; the line had been chieftains, and he himself took the royal title.
In the first year of Wei Gongdi Yanheng fled to court; Duke Dao restored him by force.
In the first year of Wei Gongdi, Yanheng lost his state and fled to court; Taizu ordered Duke Zhangwu Dao to lead troops and restore him.
The idiomatic fuses two names, drops Taizu, and drops the Zhangwu title.
In the first year of  they sent rhinoceros armor and iron mail.
In the first year of Baoding they sent rhinoceros armor and iron mail.
The idiomatic drops the reign name 保定.
Ding's younger cousin Sheng succeeded to their state.
從弟 is a younger cousin of Ding, not an unspecified cousin.
In the first year of  he asked for his family back and the emperor returned them.
In the first year of Datong, Shaoxian asked for his wife and daughters back; Taizu memorialized the Wei emperor, who returned them.
The idiomatic drops 大統, Shaoxian, Taizu, and the distinction between Taizu and the Wei emperor.
Di chief Gai Nao rebelled with allies across the region and made Nao their leader.

The Di chieftain Gai Nao and others rebelled; Nao held Beigu, his associate Tan Luo gathered in the middle of the Tao, Yang Xingde and Fu Shuang besieged Pingdi City, Jiang Fanhuai disturbed Wujie, and westward they linked with the Tanchang Qiang and Liao Gan, together raising Gai Nao as leader.
The idiomatic omits Tan Luo, Yang Xingde, Fu Shuang, Jiang Fanhuai, and Liao Gan.
Xingzhou rebels pressed Southern Qi; Zhao Chang relieved and defeated them.
Rebel Di of Xing Prefecture again pressed Southern Qi Prefecture; Governor Chiluo Xie sent an emergency appeal, and Zhao Chang led troops to the rescue and defeated them.
The idiomatic omits Governor Chiluo Xie.
He sent Liu Chongyi and Yuwen Qi, who crushed the Di and killed Jiang Duo.
He sent Liu Chongyi and Yuwen Qi, who crushed the Di and beheaded Jiang Duo and Fu Siwang.
The Grand Progenitor appointed Grand General Yuwen Gui grand commander of military affairs for six prefectures and Governor of Xing Prefecture.
Taizu appointed Grand General Yuwen Gui grand commander of military affairs for six prefectures and Governor of Xing Prefecture.
太祖 is the temple name Taizu, elsewhere rendered Emperor Wen; Grand Progenitor is an unidiomatic calque.
In Tianhe year 2 Yuwen Sheng built Yinzhou; Jihu chiefs who ambushed him were killed.
In Tianhe year 2 Yuwen Sheng built Yinzhou; the Jihu Bai Yujiu Tong and Qiao Shiluo tried to ambush him and he killed them.
The idiomatic omits the two named ambushers.
The Chinese name is 喬三勿同; Sanwu drops the last syllable.
In year 5 Liu Xiong defeated river Jihu chiefs who crossed to fight.
In year 5 Liu Xiong left Sui Prefecture to inspect the northern frontier; the river-route Jihu chiefs Qiao Bailang and Qiao Suwutong crossed the river to fight, and Xiong defeated them.
The idiomatic omits both chiefs' names.
They made Moduo, grandson of Li Sheng, Holy Martial Emperor with era Shiping.
They made Moduo, grandson of Liu Lisheng, Holy Martial Emperor with era Shiping.
劉蠡升 is Liu Lisheng; Li Sheng is a wrong surname.
Moduo held Hedong and Hexi to pinch Xian's army.
Moduo sent his associate Tianzhu to hold Hedong and his commander Muzhi to hold Hexi, planning to pinch Xian's army.
The idiomatic drops Tianzhu and Muzhi and makes Moduo the holder of both places.
Princes Jian and You broke both wings with ten thousand killed.
Prince Jian attacked Tianzhu and Prince You struck Muzhi; both were broken, with more than ten thousand heads taken.
The idiomatic omits Tianzhu and Muzhi.
In the first year of  Liu Shouluoqian rebelled; Prince Sheng captured him.
In the first year of Xuanzheng, Liu Shouluoqian rebelled; Prince Sheng captured him.
The idiomatic drops the reign name 宣政.
